UPSTREAM: soc/intel/skylake: Fix SATA booting to OS issue SATA device remains unrecognized if connected at Port 2. Port control and Status register (PCS) is by default set by hardware to the disabled state as a result of an initial power on reset. OS read PCS register during boot causes disabling of SATA ports and can't detect any devices. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:59335 TEST=Build and boot SKL from SATA device connected at Port 2. hostapd: iapp: deinitialize iapp sockets when interface down When ifconfig br-lan down, IAPP routing socket will receive RTM_DELADDR message. Fixed the issue of hostapd using 100% cpu when not checking nlmsg_type, and handled the RTM_DELADDR message by deinitializing iapp sockets. BUG=b:32684984 TEST=Tested manually by observing debug message showing received nlmsg_type, and reproduced issue without fix. Verified issue is not reproducible with the fix. Steps to reproduce: 1. Run below command in a serial console 2. ps aux | grep hostapd ; make sure hostapd is running 3. top ; verify hostapd using less than 10% CPU 4. ap-configure --wan_connection_type=bridged 5. ifconfig br-lan down 6. top ; observe hostapd using greater than 90% CPU 7. ifocnfig br-lan up 8. ap-configure --lwan_connection_type=dhcp 9. top ; observe hostapd using less than 10% CPU Change-Id: I6a32308e6de86bbcc89a9d4e04f29393d361e99a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/408733 Commit-Ready: Zhihong Yu <zhihongyu@chromium.org> Tested-by: Zhihong Yu <zhihongyu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

cr50: Overwrite the traditional GPIO controls by Cr50 console commands The following Cr50 console commands overwrite the traditional GPIOs: * Command ecrst for cold_reset; * Command sysrst for warm_reset; * Command powerbtn for pwr_button; And new ccd_ec_uart_en control is initialized to "on" to enable EC console. BUG=chrome-os-partner:58040 TEST=Connected CCD DUT and no servo-micro. Locally run inside chroot: $ cros_workon --host start hdctools $ sudo emerge hdctools $ sudo servod -c servo_v4.xml -v 0x18d1 -p 0x501b $ dut-control cold_reset warm_reset pwr_button ccd_ec_uart_en $ dut-control cold_reset:on sleep:0.2 cold_reset:off $ dut-control warm_reset:on sleep:0.2 warm_reset:off $ dut-control pwr_button:press sleep:0.2 pwr_button:release $ miniterm.py $(dut-control ec_uart_pty | cut -f2 -d:) Change-Id: Ie4d38e6d96e45d8fd65065161b7c856e7794d651 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/396613 Commit-Ready: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Tested-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Reviewed-by: Nick Sanders <nsanders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org>

fw_wp_state: Introduce abstraction of firmware write-protection Modifying the firmware protection is different on CCD-capable devices. It is done by the 'wp' command on CCD console instead of the servo pins: fw_wp_vref:some_voltage fw_wp_en:on fw_wp:on/off This CL unifies these 2 approaches by introducing a new servo control, fw_wp_state (similar to power_state). Different boards have different implementations (via servo overlay and driver). BUG=chrome-os-partner:58041 TEST=Tested on servo v3 with micro-servo and CCD. servo> dut-control fw_wp_state:force_on fw_wp_state fw_wp_state:force_on dut> crossystem wpsw_cur # Firmware WP hardware switch current position 1 servo> dut-control fw_wp_state:force_off fw_wp_state fw_wp_state:force_off dut> crossystem wpsw_cur 0 servo> dut-control fw_wp_state:reset fw_wp_state # micro-servo only fw_wp_state:off dut> crossystem wpsw_cur 0 Change-Id: If8dd7c0b07ccd820b4d956cef6cc48ba2685b320 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/397839 Commit-Ready: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Tested-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com> Reviewed-by: Todd Broch <tbroch@chromium.org>

update python paths so bin scripts work The current code creates symlinks for only the active python instance, and it links them to the main python instance. Specifically, it does: /usr/bin/python -> /usr/local/bin/python2.7 /usr/bin/python2 -> /usr/local/bin/python2.7 /usr/bin/python2.7 -> /usr/local/bin/python2.7 /usr/local/bin/python -> /usr/local/bin/python2.7 /usr/local/bin/python2 -> /usr/local/bin/python2.7 First off, it doesn't handle all python versions (like simultaneous 2.7 & 3.3), so the alternative version will remain broken (`python3.3`). It also forces `python` to always be 2.7. Most importantly though, this symlinking business is a hack to clobber the eselect wrappers so things "just work". With newer python eclasses, this no longer works all the time as programs start to use python-exec. Now, lets create symlinks in /usr/bin for all python programs that exist in /usr/local/bin. We also need a symlink for /usr/lib/python-exec to the /usr/local/lib/python-exec. This lets multiple versions of python work, and it makes newer wrapped python programs work. While we're here, also add a symlink for newer portage versions. They reworked the filesystem paths so some paths get hardcoded in the python files. [autotest] Increase MySQL connection timeout Increasing the connection timeout should make initial connection errors less likely. The default value seems to be 10 seconds (in MySQL documentation), but I think this depends on how the underlying MySQL C library was compiled. The logs in the bug suggest a timeout of ~5 seconds. Also, increase the overall timeout to 4 minutes to compensate for the increased per-try timeout. One concern is that if this is called in an RPC, the RPC response will timeout before this connection attempt. However, the existing 2 minute timeout already rules out this case. This will make the memory be allocated from atomic pool. Those allocations need big chunk of continuous memory(256KB), which may not be available after system has been running for a while and its memory get fragmented. Atomic memory pool size need be increased accrodingly. This is only an temporary sloution. The htt tx/rx struture should be created during device probe/init.
